title: Mitigation of Rapid Membrane Fouling in Dairy Wastewater Treatment Systems

sections.title: Mitigation of Rapid Membrane Fouling in Dairy Wastewater Treatment Systems
sections.problem: ReVita Water services two dairy plants near Temerin and Bečej where membrane bioreactor membranes foul faster than design assumptions, requiring full cleaning-in-place every 5 to 7 days instead of every 12 to 14 days {2}. Each full CIP consumes roughly 200 litres of citric acid and caustic solution and takes the system offline for 4 to 6 hours, resulting in significant chemical costs and lost treatment capacity over a year {2}. Seasonal patterns show fouling is worst in summer, while high fats, proteins, and sugars form a persistent gel layer {2}.
researchQuestions: What are the precise chemical and structural compositions of the foulant deposit layers accumulating on membranes at the dairy sites during summer and winter operations?
How do temperature variations and dairy wastewater constituents influence gel layer formation and transmembrane pressure spikes in membrane bioreactor systems?
Which adjustments to pre-treatment, aeration strategies, or cleaning protocols can reliably extend membrane cleaning intervals to at least twelve days?
sections.plan:
Year 1 | Characterisation of membrane foulant samples from dairy sites and identification of gel layer composition | Foulant composition report
Year 2 | Evaluation of modified pre-treatment, aeration, and cleaning-in-place protocols to extend operating intervals | Protocol optimisation report and pilot trial data

eachSideBrings.company: ReVita Water contributes historical service records, site access to the dairy plants near Temerin and Bečej, and process engineering support from its NTP Novi Sad headquarters.
eachSideBrings.faculty: The Faculty of Technology contributes membrane fouling characterisation expertise, analytical instrumentation, and cleaning protocol optimisation experience {3}.

sections.whyThisPair: ReVita Water needs specialised foulant characterisation and cleaning protocol expertise to address severe membrane fouling at regional dairy installations {2}. Ivona Bogdanović brings extensive experience in membrane fouling mechanisms, cleaning protocols, and dairy stream filtration {3}.
sections.agreedUpFront: Industrial data, service records, and foulant samples from the dairy sites will be shared under a mutual confidentiality agreement. Foreground intellectual property generated jointly will be shared, and results may be published with industry consent.

claims.text: ReVita Water designs, builds, and commission compact wastewater treatment units for food processing and pharmaceutical manufacturing plants across the region.
At two dairy plants serviced by ReVita Water, membrane bioreactor membranes foul quickly and require cleaning every week.
Ivona Bogdanović investigated sodium hydroxide and alkaline hypochlorite cleaning protocols for ultrafiltration membranes fouled with dairy process streams.
Ivona Bogdanović evaluated transmembrane pressure control strategies during continuous whey protein ultrafiltration.
Ivona Bogdanović participated in membrane-based clarification and concentration projects for regional producers.
